From the equation of a plane in the parametric form $r=p+tv+sw$, we have that its normal vector is $n=v\times w.$ In our case, the normal vectors to $Π$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & =v\times w \\  & =⟨2,0,2⟩\times ⟨1,4,0⟩ \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2 & 0 & 2 \\ 1 & 4 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 4 & 0\end{aligned}|i-|\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}|j+|\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 1 & 4\end{aligned}|k \\  & =-8i+2j+8k \\  & =⟨-8,2,8⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the plane $Π$ in dot product form is

$$
\begin{aligned}r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨-8,2,8⟩ & =⟨-15,1,1⟩\cdot ⟨-8,2,8⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨-8,2,8⟩ & =130.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, substituting $r=⟨2,3,1⟩+w⟨-3,-2,3⟩$ into the equation of the plane in dot product form, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r\cdot ⟨-8,2,8⟩ & =130 \\ ⟨2-3w,3-2w,1+3w⟩\cdot ⟨-8,2,8⟩ & =130 \\ -8(2-3w)+2(3-2w)+8(1+3w) & =130 \\ -16+24w+6-4w+8+24w & =130 \\ 44w & =132 \\ w & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to get the position vector $q$ of the intersection point $Q,$ we substitute $w=3$ into the equation of the line:

$$
\begin{aligned}q & =⟨2-3(3),3-2(3),1+3(3)⟩ \\  & =⟨-7,-3,10⟩\end{aligned}
$$

So, the intersection point is $Q(-7,-3,10).$
